text:
alex: heads-up — our main ci/deploy pipeline started failing ~20m ago with 403s when the deploy step tries to hit the +deploy API. not seeing an obvious infra outage. logs below. anyone seen this pattern?

maria: can you paste the pipeline id and the failing job id? also which cluster/region?

alex: pipeline: redwood-main/canary-deploy #3214, job: deploy-stage-2. region: us-west-2. failing step calls our internal deploy endpoint via service account token. log snippet: 
```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
content-type: application/json
{"error":"insufficient_scope","detail":"token does not have 'deploy:write'"}
```

jon: 403 w/ insufficient_scope usually means the token either rotated to a narrower scope or the token used is not the one the job refreshed to. did the job show any token refresh errors earlier in the log?

alex: earlier there was a refresh attempt, followed by a 200, then ~25m later these 403s start. full trace: 
```
[00:00:01] obtaining token from /secrets/ephemeral
[00:00:02] token acquired, scopes: deploy:write,deploy:read
[00:27:40] making deploy call -> 200
[00:52:12] making deploy call -> 403 insufficient_scope
```

maria: pinging @rita (infra) and @secrets-bot in case there's a platform change. :pray:

secrets-bot: notice — service-account-ephemeral rotation policy changed by infra-config-bot at 2026-02-14T03:12:11Z. previous ttl: 12h; new ttl: 30m.

rita (infra): yep — we rolled a change last night to tighten ephemeral SA lifetimes to 30m for higher-risk projects. it looks like this pipeline's jobs run ~45-60m, so tokens are expiring mid-job and when the job tries to refresh it's getting a shorter-scope fallback token due to an enforcement check. root cause likely the TTL + refresh path not refreshing scopes correctly.

jon: quick question — when the job refreshes, is it requesting the same scope set? or is there an interactive step that requests elevated scope and falls back on failure?

alex: our handler calls the token refresh endpoint with the required scopes. but it seems the refresh returned a token missing deploy:write. curl from the job container shows: 
```
curl -sS -X POST https://secrets.internal/api/refresh -d '{"scopes":["deploy:write","deploy:read"]}' -H "Authorization: Bearer <old-token>" | jq .
{"access_token":"...","scopes":["deploy:read"],"expires_in":1783}
```

rita (infra): that's the smoking gun. the refresh flow is hitting the new policy enforcement which denies re-issuing long-lived scope sets for tokens past the new TTL window and returns a minimal-scoped token.

maria: ok — we need an immediate mitigation for customers hitting CI failures. thoughts?

rita (infra): mitigation options (short-term):
- revert the TTL change on the affected org(s) -> roll back policy (fast, but reduces security posture).
- patch the token refresh service to preserve requested scopes for active refreshes that originated before policy change (targeted, slightly more work).
- adjust pipelines to explicitly re-request a fresh token before the deploy step (workaround).

jon: for the shortest TTR, revert the policy for the redwood-main org and create a scoped rollback. i'll take that if infra + security ok.

support-alex: customer-impacted list: multiple internal prod pipelines and several customers using long-running CI jobs. we should notify customers and add a deploy-blocker tag. :warning:

rita (infra): i'm +1 on targeted rollback for orgs with active long-running pipelines. will open an infra rollback change and patch the policy to exclude orgs with the "ci-long-jobs" flag.

alex: thanks. can you also add a short-term pipeline change we can do immediately? i'll add a job pre-step that forces token refresh within 5m of deploy so token is fresh for the step. repo snippet: 
```
- run: refresh-token --scopes "deploy:write deploy:read"
- run: deploy --target canary
```

maria: action items: 
1) @rita open rollback/change (infra) — ETA 45m
2) @alex add pre-deploy refresh step and PR to pipeline templates — ETA 15m
3) @jon add monitoring alert for 401/403 surge on deploy endpoints and a runbook entry — ETA 1h
4) @support-alex draft customer comms and update support tickets — ETA 30m

rita (infra): started rollback change CL-3981, will update when done. will also add an audit log entry to track which orgs are exempted.

jon: quick note: we should also add an automated test to the pipeline templates that simulates mid-job refresh to catch regressions. filing ticket.

secrets-bot: audit — token-policy change author: infra-config-bot, change-id: cfg-2026-0214-07, affected: 142 orgs; rollback pending for org: redwood-main.

alex: re-run of failed job after adding pre-refresh succeeded (manual test) — deploy returned 200.

maria: closing the escalation once rollback done and customers notified. great job triaging quickly. :tada:

rita (infra): rollback completed at 2026-02-14T04:12:09Z. leaving a follow-up to propose safer default TTLs and a migration window.

support-alex: filed customer note and escalations summary, linking ticket SR-8792. copying the mitigation steps in the ticket.

alex: moving to postmortem and next steps: add regression test in pipeline templates, update docs to call out token expiry windows, and coordinate a migration plan before we re-tighten TTLs.

maria: assigning postmortem owners: alex (investigation + repro), rita (policy + infra changes), jon (monitoring + runbook), support-alex (customer comms). thanks everyone.
